_comment: Claims register for the Jordan's Principle page. A parent acts on this for a child who needs something now, so the routing and the eligibility boundary matter more than the history.
pageTitle: My child needs something. Who pays for it?

claims.claim: Where there is a jurisdictional dispute about who pays, the government of first contact pays and settles the billing afterwards.
claims.note: PRIORITY. This is the answer strip and the whole point of the page, and it could not be confirmed in these words on ISC's own page. Confirm the plain-language statement is accurate.

claims.claim: Jordan's Principle is for First Nations children. Requests for Inuit children go through the Inuit Child First Initiative.
claims.note: GAP FOUND. ISC routes Inuit children separately and neither this page nor /money/asking said so, which would send an Inuit parent to the wrong door. Being fixed alongside this register.

claims.claim: In 2016 the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal found Canada's approach discriminatory and ordered it to implement the full meaning and scope of Jordan's Principle.
claims.sourceQuote: In 2016, the CHRT determined the Government of Canada's approach...was discriminatory ... ordered the Government of Canada to implement the full meaning and scope

claims.claim: This is a legal obligation backed by a human rights ruling, not a discretionary grant programme that can be cut.
claims.note: Consequential framing — it is what tells a parent to persist after a refusal. Confirm it is accurate as stated.

claims.claim: The Jordan's Principle call centre is 1-855-572-4453 and operates at all hours.
claims.sourceQuote: 1-855-JP-CHILD (1-855-572-4453) ... 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

claims.claim: Jordan River Anderson was a boy from Norway House Cree Nation in Manitoba.
Jordan was born in 1999, spent more than two years in hospital for non-medical reasons, and died in 2005 aged five.
claims.note: Widely reported and not confirmable on ISC's page. It is the emotional core of the page, so if any detail is wrong it should be corrected rather than removed.

claims.claim: In 2007 the House of Commons unanimously passed a motion supporting Jordan's Principle.
A request can cover something the family has already paid for.
claims.note: Stated on /money/asking as well as here. Confirm, because it changes whether a parent bothers to ask about past costs.
